title: GlowPath
seoIntro: GlowPath is a swipe puzzle about lighting every active square from one starting point without wasting the route.
seoDetails: GlowPath turns each board into a clean pathfinding challenge. Start on the pulsing entry tile, swipe through adjacent squares, backtrack when needed, and finish when every active tile glows.
seoHowToPlay: Press the starting tile, then swipe through unlit neighboring tiles. Holes are blocked, revisiting a lit tile is ignored unless it is the previous square, and a completed route lights the whole stage.
seoFeatures: Start from the pulsing entry square
Swipe through each active tile exactly once
Backtrack one step to repair a route without restarting
designNotes: The useful move in GlowPath is often the one that preserves exits. Watch corners and narrow bridges before committing, because a bright-looking route can still strand an unlit square.
controls: Tap the pulsing start tile to begin
Swipe or drag into adjacent active tiles
Swipe into the previous tile to undo the last step
playerTips: Trace the forced corners before lighting the middle
Use backtracking immediately when a route traps itself
Leave branching areas flexible until the path shape is clear

guideSections.heading: Who GlowPath Is For
guideSections.copy: GlowPath fits players who like compact logic puzzles with a tactile swipe rhythm. Each stage is short, readable, and built around finding one continuous route through the lit squares.

guideSections.heading: Reading the Board
guideSections.copy: Look for dead ends, corners, and narrow connectors before you start moving quickly. Strong routes usually handle constrained tiles first, then use open space to connect the remaining squares.

guideSections.heading: Using Backtrack
guideSections.copy: Backtracking is not a penalty. If the route blocks itself, swipe into the previous square, turn off the last tile, and correct the path while the board shape is still fresh.

faq.question: What kind of puzzle is GlowPath?
faq.answer: GlowPath is a path puzzle where you light every active square by swiping a continuous route from the starting tile.

faq.question: Can I undo a move in GlowPath?
faq.answer: Yes. Swipe back into the previous square to turn off the last tile and continue from there.

title: ScrollSort
seoIntro: ScrollSort is a reading-and-sorting puzzle about catching the active rule before the list gets away from you.
seoDetails: ScrollSort is built around quick classification. Each round asks you to read the prompt, identify what belongs together, and sort confidently instead of hesitating over every item.
seoHowToPlay: Start by naming the sorting rule out loud in your head, then move through the list in batches. If an item does not fit the current rule, skip it for a moment and come back once the obvious matches are cleared.
seoFeatures: Read the current sorting rule before moving items
Group obvious matches first
Use later passes for edge cases instead of stalling

faq.question: What kind of puzzle is ScrollSort?
faq.answer: ScrollSort is a sorting puzzle about reading a rule quickly and organizing items that match it.

faq.question: What should I practice first in ScrollSort?
faq.answer: Practice clearing the obvious matches first so you do not lose time debating every borderline item.

title: LumaRush
seoIntro: LumaRush is a tap puzzle about clearing connected groups of matching colors.
seoDetails: Tap a group of matching tiles connected horizontally or vertically to clear it. Tiles fall into the gaps and the board refills, creating new groups to spot.
seoHowToPlay: Find at least three matching tiles joined along their edges, then tap or click any tile in that group. For your first move, look for a row of three matching colors and tap one of them; diagonal neighbors do not connect.
seoFeatures: Clear connected groups of matching colors
Watch tiles fall and refill the board
Find larger groups before committing
designNotes: Read the whole connected group before tapping. Clearing one group changes the neighboring tiles, so check the new board after each move.
controls: Tap or click any tile in a connected matching group
Match at least three tiles connected horizontally or vertically
playerTips: Look for edge-connected colors rather than diagonal matches
Check the board again after tiles fall
Compare nearby groups before choosing a move

guideSections.heading: Reading connected groups
guideSections.copy: Matching colors connect through shared edges. Start with a group of three or more and tap any member to clear the group.

guideSections.heading: After a clear
guideSections.copy: Tiles fall and new tiles refill the gaps. Recheck the new connections before your next tap.

faq.question: Can I play LumaRush instantly in my browser?
faq.answer: Yes. LumaRush loads directly in your browser without a separate install.

faq.question: Is fullscreen available for LumaRush?
faq.answer: Yes. Use the Full Screen link on the game page for an expanded play view.

title: Racer
seoIntro: Racer is a browser kart-racing game with toy-scale tracks, quick laps, and multiplayer-ready race sessions.
seoDetails: Racer rewards clean lines more than frantic steering. The fun is learning a toy-scale track corner by corner, finding where to ease off, and carrying a smoother exit into the next stretch.
seoHowToPlay: Take the first lap as scouting. Learn where the sharp turns, ramps, and boost windows are, then retry with one cleaner section as your goal.
seoFeatures: Learn one corner before chasing a full fast lap
Brake or ease off before sharp turns
Use boost only when the exit is lined up
designNotes: If you are sliding wide, you probably started the turn too late. Slow down before the corner, aim for a clean exit, and let speed come from rhythm instead of correction.
controls: Use arrow keys or WASD-style movement controls on desktop
Use fullscreen mode for the most stable view of the track
Keep steering inputs deliberate through corners before accelerating out
playerTips: Brake or ease off before sharp turns instead of correcting late
Learn one track section at a time before chasing full-run speed
Use early laps to find boost timing and cleaner racing lines

guideSections.heading: Who Racer Is For
guideSections.copy: Racer fits players who like short, repeatable racing sessions where improvement comes from cleaner turns and better track memory. It is built for quick browser access rather than long setup or downloads.

guideSections.heading: Learning the Track
guideSections.copy: Strong runs start with reading the next corner early. Keep the kart stable before entering a turn, then accelerate once the exit is clear instead of overcorrecting midway through the corner.

guideSections.heading: What to Practice First
guideSections.copy: Racer is easiest to enjoy when you treat each lap as practice. Pick one corner, ramp, or boost window to improve, then restart and try to carry that cleaner line through the full run.

faq.question: Can I play Racer in the browser?
faq.answer: Yes. Racer opens directly from Terapixel Games in a modern browser.

faq.question: What should I practice first in Racer?
faq.answer: Start with clean steering through corners. A steady line is more useful than chasing speed before you know the track.

title: Wormhole Raiders
seoIntro: Wormhole Raiders is a survival action game about diving through unstable space, reading enemy pressure, and taking the opening before it collapses.
seoDetails: Wormhole Raiders is about controlled aggression. You are not just dodging; you are choosing when to cut through danger, when to hold distance, and when a wormhole gives you enough room to reset the fight.
seoHowToPlay: Keep your eyes on the next safe pocket, then move before the screen closes in. Use wormholes and open space to break pressure instead of drifting into the edge of the arena.
seoFeatures: Use wormholes to escape collapsing pressure
Read enemy movement before committing
Survive longer by resetting into open space

faq.question: What type of game is Wormhole Raiders?
faq.answer: Wormhole Raiders is a survival action game about using movement and wormholes to stay alive under pressure.

faq.question: What should I watch in Wormhole Raiders?
faq.answer: Watch where pressure is closing in, then move toward open space before the escape route disappears.

title: Color Crunch
seoIntro: Color Crunch is a 4×4 swipe-and-merge puzzle about combining equal tiles into higher levels.
seoDetails: Slide the whole board in one direction. Equal-level tiles merge into the next level, and a successful move adds a new tile. Keep space open so the board has room to move.
seoHowToPlay: Swipe up, down, left, or right, drag with the left mouse button, or use arrow keys or WASD. For a first merge, find two equal tiles in a row and slide toward that row’s edge so they meet.
seoFeatures: Slide a 4×4 board in four directions
Merge equal-level tiles into higher levels
Keep empty spaces available for new tiles
designNotes: Each input moves the board as a whole. Plan where equal tiles will meet and where the new tile can leave space for another move.
controls: Arrow keys or WASD slide the board
Swipe on touch screens, or hold the left mouse button and drag, then release
playerTips: Line up equal-level tiles before sliding
Leave empty cells for new tiles
Check the whole board before choosing a direction

guideSections.heading: Sliding the board
guideSections.copy: Every swipe moves all tiles toward one edge. Equal tiles that meet combine into a higher-level tile.

guideSections.heading: Keeping room to merge
guideSections.copy: Successful moves spawn a new tile. Preserve open cells and plan the next merge before filling the board.

faq.question: How do I control Color Crunch?
faq.answer: Use arrow keys, WASD, a touch swipe, or a left-mouse drag to slide the 4×4 board.

faq.question: What is the goal?
faq.answer: Merge equal tiles into higher levels while keeping legal moves available.

title: Block Forge
seoIntro: Block Forge is a placement puzzle about fitting block pieces cleanly while keeping the board open for the next shape.
seoDetails: Block Forge rewards players who think two pieces ahead. A strong board is not just full of completed lines; it has flexible gaps, clean corners, and enough breathing room for awkward shapes.
seoHowToPlay: Place each block where it clears space or preserves future options. Avoid creating one-cell holes, keep the center flexible, and save wide open areas for pieces that are hard to fit.
seoFeatures: Place pieces without trapping small gaps
Build clears while preserving open board space
Plan around awkward shapes before they arrive

faq.question: What makes Block Forge different from casual puzzle games?
faq.answer: Block Forge is about piece placement and board control, so the best moves preserve space instead of only chasing the first clear.

faq.question: What is the main mistake in Block Forge?
faq.answer: The main mistake is creating tiny dead spaces that future pieces cannot use.

title: SumSlide
seoIntro: SumSlide is a number puzzle about sliding tiles into useful totals without wasting moves.
seoDetails: SumSlide turns arithmetic into route planning. Each move changes the board, so good solutions come from seeing which numbers can combine cleanly and which slide will set up the next sum.
seoHowToPlay: Find the target total first, then trace which tiles can reach it with the fewest slides. Move numbers only when the path creates a sum or opens a better lane for the next one.
seoFeatures: Build target sums from movable number tiles
Plan slide paths before committing
Replay boards to reduce wasted moves

faq.question: What is the goal in SumSlide?
faq.answer: The goal is to combine number tiles into the needed sums while using clean slide paths.

faq.question: What skills does SumSlide focus on?
faq.answer: SumSlide focuses on mental arithmetic, path planning, and recognizing efficient number combinations.

title: Worm Breaker
seoIntro: Worm Breaker is a cylindrical tunnel brickbreaker with a paddle that rotates around the tunnel wall.
seoDetails: Rotate the glowing paddle to rebound the ball into bricks deeper in the tunnel. Track the returning ball around the cylinder and bring the paddle into its path before it passes you.
seoHowToPlay: Use Left/Right or A/D to rotate the paddle, or press and drag horizontally on a touch screen. Start by making a small rotation, then track the ball’s return and line up a rebound to send it back toward the bricks.
seoFeatures: Rotate a paddle around a cylindrical tunnel
Rebound the ball into tunnel bricks
Track the ball’s angle on its return
designNotes: The paddle moves around the tunnel rather than across a flat screen. Watch the ball’s angular position as it returns and adjust early to meet it.
controls: Left/Right arrow keys or A/D rotate the paddle
On touch screens, press and drag horizontally; release to stop steering
playerTips: Follow the ball around the tunnel wall
Adjust the paddle before the ball reaches you
Use small corrections to line up a rebound

guideSections.heading: Rotating the paddle
guideSections.copy: Use Left/Right or A/D, or horizontal touch dragging, to move the paddle around the cylinder.

guideSections.heading: Returning the ball
guideSections.copy: Meet the returning ball with the paddle to bounce it into the tunnel bricks. Missing below the paddle loses the ball.

faq.question: What is the goal in Worm Breaker?
faq.answer: Rebound the ball with a rotating paddle to break bricks inside a cylindrical tunnel.

faq.question: Which keyboard controls are supported?
faq.answer: Left/Right arrows and A/D rotate the paddle. Touch screens support horizontal dragging.

title: GloBlocks
seoIntro: GloBlocks is a luminous block puzzle about placing glowing shapes, setting up clears, and keeping the board from choking itself.
seoDetails: GloBlocks is slower and more deliberate than a reaction game. The useful move is often the one that keeps future shapes playable, even if another placement scores sooner.
seoHowToPlay: Study the incoming shapes before placing the first one. Keep edges clean, avoid isolated gaps, and set up clears that leave the board easier to use afterward.
seoFeatures: Place glowing shapes with future pieces in mind
Set up clears that open the board
Avoid isolated holes that break later placements

faq.question: What kind of game is GloBlocks?
faq.answer: GloBlocks is a block placement puzzle about fitting glowing shapes while preserving board space.

faq.question: What should I focus on in GloBlocks?
faq.answer: Focus on keeping the board flexible, especially around edges and corners where bad gaps are hard to repair.

title: SpeedSolitaire
seoIntro: SpeedSolitaire is a fast browser card game that blends classic solitaire logic with time-focused play.
seoDetails: SpeedSolitaire keeps the familiar card logic but makes hesitation visible. Better runs come from exposing hidden cards early, recognizing obvious moves faster, and avoiding side moves that slow the whole board down.
seoHowToPlay: Start by opening hidden cards when the move is clean. Keep foundations moving when it helps, but do not chase every possible move if it breaks your flow.
seoFeatures: Expose hidden cards early
Move quickly when the next play is obvious
Practice one habit per run, like fewer pauses or cleaner stacks
designNotes: SpeedSolitaire keeps the familiar solitaire structure but frames each session around pace. The best runs come from reducing pauses, recognizing card movement options early, and avoiding unnecessary backtracking.
controls: Use mouse, trackpad, or touch input to move cards
Use fullscreen mode when practicing time-focused runs
Pause only when needed; repeated short runs build faster recognition
playerTips: Expose hidden cards as early as possible when the move is clean
Do not chase every possible move if it slows the whole run
Practice one session goal at a time, such as fewer hesitations or faster foundation moves

guideSections.heading: Who SpeedSolitaire Is For
guideSections.copy: SpeedSolitaire is for card players who know the comfort of classic solitaire but want a sharper pace. It is useful for short daily practice because each run gives clear feedback on hesitation, missed card flow, and decision speed.

guideSections.heading: Playing for Time
guideSections.copy: Fast runs are not only about moving every card immediately. The better habit is to expose hidden cards, keep foundations moving when it costs little time, and avoid side moves that create more searching later.

guideSections.heading: Improving Without Guessing
guideSections.copy: Pick one goal per session: fewer pauses, faster opening moves, cleaner stack management, or more consistent endgame flow. Practicing one behavior at a time makes progress easier to notice than simply replaying until a lucky layout appears.

faq.question: How is SpeedSolitaire different from regular solitaire?
faq.answer: SpeedSolitaire keeps classic solitaire foundations but emphasizes faster decisions and shorter completion times.

faq.question: Can I use SpeedSolitaire for daily practice?
faq.answer: Yes. Short rounds make it useful for regular score and time improvement sessions.
